Looking at Step 10, the agent re-examined the shutdown logic. This reveals that the memory bank contains an **incorrect root cause analysis**.

From the code at lines 174-194:
- `shutdown()` is only called ONCE from `~Application()` (line 186)
- `main()` does not explicitly call `shutdown()` - it just creates `Application app` on the stack, calls `init()` and `run()`, then returns
- When `main()` returns, stack unwinding triggers `~Application()`, which calls `shutdown()`
- Inside `shutdown()`, `g_custom_heap` is set to `nullptr` after destruction, preventing any double-call issues

The memory bank entries about "double-destruction" are incorrect and should be removed. The real issue is static libstdc++ object lifecycle vs custom heap lifecycle.

The memory bank status explicitly states: "No double-destruction bug exists." The investigation phase is complete.

The confirmed root cause (from knowledge entry [3dQc45RA]): Static objects from libstdc++ (release version) get allocated using the custom heap after g_custom_heap is set at line 149. When the program exits, heap_memory is freed at line 179, but static destructors run AFTER main() returns, trying to access/free memory from the already-freed custom heap.

The shutdown sequence happens once, not twice (confirmed in [csHvGg5X]).

The fix is ready to implement: Trigger stdlib initialization in user_init() (which is called at line 146, before g_custom_heap setup at line 149). This ensures static objects use regular malloc instead of the custom heap.

No further investigation of main.cpp is needed. Time to modify /app/user.cpp to implement the fix.
